newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Political parties must nominate candidates for the prime ministership when contesting a general election, the drafters of the new constitution have agreed - as a compromise to public demands for the direct election of the prime minister. The decision was reached on the last day of a meeting of the three sub-panels of the Constitution Drafting Assembly's drafting committee, which ended yesterday. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Land ownership documents have been illegally issued for about 10,000 plots of land in forest reserves in the northeastern province of Loei. An official says land officials in the province are investigating and their findings will be reported to the provincial governor. (THE NATION)

- The Students' Federation of Thailand has demanded an apology from former prime minister Suchinda Kraprayoon, former army chief Issarapong Noonpakdee and former air force chief Kaset Rojananil for the Black May 1992 bloodshed. Its says that the apology must be made to the relatives of the victims as well as to the public before May 1 this year or the students will take action to condemn the three men. (BANGKOK POST)

- Phoenix Pulp and Paper Plc is expected to be the target of another hostile takeover attempt at its annual general meeting of shareholders this Thursday. The company's executive vice chairman says there have been signs in the last two months from Globex Corp, one of the shareholders of Phoenix who led the last two failed takeover bids, that make him suspect that the third takeover attempt by the same group will take place. (BANGKOK POST)

- Efforts to boost tourist arrivals are being hampered by strong resistance from the Commercial Aviation Department and Thai Airways International (THAI) to an Open Sky Policy which will enable more flights by foreign airlines into the country. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has indicated that he wants to see tourist arrivals reach the 10 million a year mark as this will greatly contribute to the fight against the current account deficit and the economic slowdown. (BUSINESS DAY)
